To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TOC is a heterogeneous disorder with a multifactorial etiology, that the most common clinical features are the fear of contamination, the doubts and the need for symmetry, and that the most common etiologic factors are the genetic and the neurobiological ones.

the OCD dimensions of contamination, doubt, symmetry and hoarding are related to different etiopathogenic factors, clinical courses and treatment responses, suggesting the need to develop specific treatment approaches based on these dimensions.

the most common symptoms of OCS in OCD patients are contamination fears and doubts, that the most common compulsions are cleaning and checking, that the presence of obsessions and compulsions is associated with greater severity of OCD, and that the presence of both obsessions and compulsion is associated with greater OCD severity than either obsessions or compulsions alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the clinical features of OCD and their relation to etiopathogenic, course, and long-term outcome factors.
the study of the cognitive and affective processes that are involved in the generation and maintenance of obsessive-compulsive symptoms.
the study of the cognitive processes that underlie obsessive-compulsive symptoms and the relationship between these symptoms and anxiety.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the etiological factors of OCD include a combination of genetic and environmental factors, and that OCD is characterized by a complex and multifactorial neurobiology.

the etiopathogenesis of OCD is complex and not fully understood, and that the neurochemical, neuroanatomic, and neurophysiologic abnormalities that may be present in OCD patients are not specific to the disease and are also seen in other anxiety and mood disorders.
the etiopathogenic mechanisms underlying the OCD are complex and multifactorial, and that the current knowledge of them is still limited and incomplete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a significant correlation between the dimensions and symptomatology of the obsessive-compulsive spectrum, as well as between the dimensions and etiopathogenic factors, clinical course and long term response in patients with obsessive compulsive disorder.
the OCD patients with a high degree of contamination fear and washing compulsions have a more severe disease course and a worse prognosis than patients with a high level of checking compulsions.

we have developed and validated a new instrument to assess the quality of life in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) that is easy to administer, and that is sensitive and responsive in clinical trials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical presentation of OCD is heterogeneous and that the clinical subtypes of OCD are associated with different neurobiological mechanisms.

we need to be careful about the way we interpret our data, and the results of others, when it comes to the association between OCD and ADHD, and the possible implications of this association for treatment.
